newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU officials tie up details of set-aside penalties.
newsitem.headline: EU officials tie up details of set-aside penalties.

text.p: European Union member state agricultural officials finalised details of a political deal struck last week in Luxembourg easing cereals set-aside penalties for exceeding planting limits, EU officials said.
They said that the text would soon be formally approved at an EU ministerial meeting.
The deal on set-aside penalties, which was part of the 1997/98 farm price package, exempted farmers in countries which were hit by drought or floods, notably Spain, from the area limits.
It met German demands to target penalties on regions which over-planted, instead of penalising the whole country.
Countries would also be allowed to penalise individual farms. But Ireland, which requested the change, would have to change its 1989/91 reference years to a more recent period.
Under EU regulation 1765/92, farmers who overshoot base areas either have to set aside extra land the following year or pay financial penalties.
Spain opposed the overall price package because its demands on regional cereals yields and milk fat content were rejected on cost grounds.
